questions.stem: A surveyor walks 135 km east, turns right and walks 240 km, then turns right and walks 7 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 272. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 128 km along the initial direction and 240 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(128² + 240²) = 272 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 78 km north, turns right and walks 105 km, then turns right and walks 22 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 119. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 56 km along the initial direction and 105 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(56² + 105²) = 119 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 74 km west, turns right and walks 68 km, then turns right and walks 23 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 85. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 51 km along the initial direction and 68 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(51² + 68²) = 85 km.

questions.stem:
Statements: W < U < X > Q = V.
Conclusions: I. U ≥ V   II. X > W.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem: In a queue of 44 candidates, a candidate is 15th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 26. New front rank = 15+4 = 19. Back rank = 44 − 19 + 1 = 26.

questions.stem: In a queue of 60 candidates, a candidate is 12th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 46. New front rank = 12+3 = 15. Back rank = 60 − 15 + 1 = 46.

questions.stem:
Statements: No lockers is a accounts. Some accounts are deposits. All deposits are cheques.
Conclusions:
I. All lockers are cheques.
II. Some cheques are accounts.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some lockers are accounts. All accounts are deposits. No deposits is a cheques.
Conclusions:
I. Some lockers are deposits.
II. Some accounts are cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few lockers are accounts. All accounts are deposits. No deposits is a cheques.
Conclusions:
I. Some lockers are not accounts.
II. No accounts is a cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:

I. All lockers are cheques.

questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem: H is the brother of G. G is the mother of F. D is the father of H and G. How is H related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. H is the brother of F’s mother G. Therefore H is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: A is the mother of C. G is the son of C. F is the father of C. How is G related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. F is a parent of C, and G is C’s son. Hence G is F’s grandchild.

questions.stem: G is the only daughter of F. F is the father of G. E is the son of G. A is the sister of F. How is F related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. F is the father of G, and G is E’s mother. Thus F is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
savings banking access = vo ze pa
savings growth rural = re ze ni
banking growth digital = vo re su
access rural digital = pa su ni
savings banking digital = su ze vo
What is the code for “access”?
questions.explanation: Answer: pa. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: savings = ze, banking = vo, access = pa, growth = re, rural = ni, digital = su.

questions.explanation: Answer: 22 : 27. questions.stem: [Caselet set] What is the total number in the male category at A and C together?
questions.explanation: Answer: 660. Derived data: A: first category 240, second category 360; B: first category 640, second category 480; C: first category 420, second category 560; D: first category 960, second category 640; E: first category 660, second category 440. 240 + 420 = 660.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] A new branch F has a total equal to the average total at A and E. Its categories are split in ratio 2:3. What is the number in its second category?
questions.explanation: Answer: 510. Derived data: A: first category 240, second category 360; B: first category 640, second category 480; C: first category 420, second category 560; D: first category 960, second category 640; E: first category 660, second category 440. Average total = (total A + total E)/2. The second category is 3/5 of that average.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] The female category at D is what percentage of the male category at B? (Round to two decimal places.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 100. Derived data: A: first category 240, second category 360; B: first category 640, second category 480; C: first category 420, second category 560; D: first category 960, second category 640; E: first category 660, second category 440. 640 ÷ 640 × 100 = 100%.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1300. It is marked above cost and sold at a 25% discount on marked price, earning 20% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 2080. Selling price = 1300 × 120/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.75 = 2080.
